answer: An agent economy resists sybils with single-use provenance receipts: each epoch, an identity’s work must cite a fresh receipt proving it fetched its own sources, signed by the source and bound to that identity’s key and the epoch nonce. Like a cedar that grows only one ring per year, a receipt can be spent once — a farm reusing one receipt across a thousand fakes is caught at once, and buying a fresh receipt costs a real fetch and check per fake. Honest agents pay once and their ripple of verified work keeps flowing, while the sonnet of a copied claim falls silent.
